sasha: Heads-up — I sketched a lightweight follow-up to the prefix-caching eviction discussion. Proposal: introduce a small per-shard 'spill queue' that serializes demote work for large prefixes and keeps a short-lived demote token. This avoids noisy bulk demotes during reclaim. Thoughts?
ken: can you TL;DR the benefits vs just rate-limiting demote ops?
sasha: tl;dr: rate-limit still causes thundering when many prefixes cross threshold. Spill queue lets us: 1) batch demotes for contiguous key ranges, 2) attach a demote-token -> which prevents duplicate demote jobs, 3) combine soft->hard transitions with a single atomic marker so readers see a single transition point.
nate: sounds promising. how do we ensure correctness for in-flight reads that hold a prefix lease while demote runs?
sasha: idea: demote-token carries a monotonic generation id. Lease checks compare generation; if read's lease generation < active demote generation, readers either 1) return stale-but-valid with marker, or 2) fetch from remote and fast-fail local cache. We need to pick fallback behavior.
olivia: for safety I'd prefer conservative: if mismatch, fall back to authoritative KV read. Simpler to reason about and avoids subtle staleness. Performance hit but correctness.
ken: do we have metrics to measure impact? what about heavy hotkeys where fallback kills p95?
sasha: yep that's the tradeoff. Option B: serve stale with an "eviction-in-progress" header and let client decide. Might be ok for low-SLA tenants. Need tenant QoS tagging.
ate: can we attach per-tenant policy so dedicated tenants always get strict correctness (fallback to authoritative) and PLG tenants can accept stale?
sasha: exactly. config sketch: 
```
cache.eviction.spill_queue.enabled = true
cache.eviction.spill_queue.max_inflight = 64
cache.eviction.generation_policy = "per-prefix" # or global
cache.eviction.tenant_policy.default = "serve-stale"
cache.eviction.tenant_policy.enterprise = "strict-fallback"
```
ken: how heavy is the coordination? does every shard need to talk to a central coordinator to get a demote-token?
sasha: no central coordinator. spill queue is local to shard. Token is just a small in-memory lease with (prefix, generation, expiry). When a demote needs to be scheduled, we TryAcquire on the token. If another shard needs to demote overlapping prefix, it uses a light handshake: RPC to owner shard to request coalesce. Owner can accept and add request to its local queue.
olivia: owner-based coalesce seems fine. We should define a timebox so ownership doesn't stall (e.g., token TTL 250ms). Also backoff rules for retries.
nate: edge-case: prefix split or migration while demote in-flight. How do we avoid double-demote or lost data?
sasha: plan: token carries the shard-id and an epoch. On split/migrate we bump epoch and migrate token state as part of the handoff. If token owner disappears, tokens expire and other shards can attempt a takeover. We'll add a guarded handoff RPC that does stable transfer (write-ahead handoff entry) so we can detect races.
ken: that sounds like reintroducing a sequencer. Are we ok with the extra complexity?
sasha: minimal sequencer-like behavior but bounded: only for demote-tokens, TTL-based and owner-local first. No global ordering.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary cluster build queued (eviction-spill-queue) — will run tests on prefix_handshake and demote_inflight suites.
olivia: operational checklist: 1) metrics: demote-coalesced, demote-fallback-rate, stale-served-rate, token-takeover-count 2) toggles: global kill-switch + per-tenant policy 3) canary to PLG-only before enterprise 4) run canary under high-surge test.
nate: one more thought: add a verification step post-demote that asserts no active leases with older generation exist (scan a sample). If violation discovered, we can trigger read-repair across affected prefixes. Might be heavy, but run only in debug mode.
sasha: agreed — will add a debug verifier flag. I'll open a short RFC and include the config, handshake APIs, and tests. Can someone volunteer to review for correctness/telemetry?
ken: I can review correctness and failure modes.
olivia: I'll take telemetry and rollout plan.
nate: I'll sanity-check canary tests and add a few stress scenarios.
sasha: thanks — will post RFC link here once live. For now: plan to prototype a local-only spill_queue impl behind feature flag. Minimal API: `TryAcquireDemoteToken(prefix) -> (acquired, generation)` and `RequestCoalesce(prefix, owner_shard)` RPC.
ken: SGTM. small nit: make generation a 64-bit monotonic counter to avoid wrap issues.
sasha: yep. Also track demote_reason tag (evict_due_to_slab, tenant_spill, manual). Adds observability.
olivia: :thumbsup:

sasha: cool — will follow up after prototype tests. Thanks everyone.
